units.title: Switch clients from Hotjar to Microsoft Clarity when heatmap and recording needs are equivalent

claim.text: The source says that at the time of recording Microsoft Clarity was completely free and had no data limit, so as much data as wanted could be collected, in contrast to Hotjar's tiered pricing.
claim.quote: at the time of this recording Microsoft Clarity is completely free right so there's no data limit whatsoever you can collect as much data as you want

action.text: The source says they are moving a lot of clients from Hotjar over to Clarity solely for the cost reason, because the two do the same thing for heatmaps and recording.
action.quote: we're kind of in the process of move a lot of clients over from hot to Clarity solely for that reason because they pretty much do the same thing when it comes to heat MPP and recording

args.text: Clients with 300,000 to 400,000 visitors per month accumulate a large Hotjar bill.
args.quote: for a lot of our cro clients they get 300,000 to 400,000 visitors per month um and so that build tends to rack up quite a bit

args.text: Even small clients want to extract as much value as possible from their traffic.
args.quote: you really want to extract as much value from your traffic

args.text: An all-in-one platform covering heatmaps, recordings, user interviews, surveys and funnels is wanted, in which case the source favours Hotjar.
args.quote: if you're looking for um a solution that contains an all-in-one platform right so the ability to look at heat Maps recordings uh user interviews surveys and funnels all in one Tool uh then hotra would be your best bet

unknowns: The source describes the client migration as in process, not complete.
Clarity being free with no data limit is stated as of the time of this recording, not as a current fact.

units.title: Clarity and Hotjar overlap on the core behaviour analytics features

claim.text: The source says Hotjar pretty much does the exact same thing as Clarity and that most user-behaviour tools are very similar in recording and heatmap functionality.
claim.quote: Hot D pretty much does the exact same thing and most of these user Behavior tools do very similar things in that regard

unknowns: The source does not address whether the tools differ in data capture, sampling or retention beyond what the video covers.

units.title: Inspect Clarity area maps to see where clicks are diverted

claim.text: The source describes area maps in Microsoft Clarity as showing effectively the percentage of clicks that go to different parts of the website.
claim.quote: the ability to look at area maps right so you're actually able to see you know effectively the percentage of clicks that go to different um parts of the website

action.text: Look at the click percentages in the area map, including clicks on the navigation, to see where attention is being diverted.
action.quote: I can see 5.9% of clicks go here I can look at the clicks on the navigation um and you're able to see you know where is the tension kind of being diverted to

args.text: The source frames area maps as seeing where people are clicking in the first place.
args.quote: just seeing where people are clicking in the first place

unknowns: No threshold or decision rule is given for interpreting area map click percentages.
The source does not state whether area maps need a minimum traffic volume.

units.title: Area map finding on a client site: high-click section few visitors reached

claim.text: On a client site, 10.41% of clicks went to the shop-by-industry section further down the page while only 30 to 35% of people actually reached that section.
claim.quote: we saw that 10.41% of clicks were going towards the shop by industry section that was kind of further down the page but you know only 30 to 35% of people were actually reaching this section

action.text: The source ran a simple A/B test putting those same icons at the top of the homepage to send people into the collection pages and further down the funnel.
action.quote: we ran a simple AB test where we actually put those same icons at the top of the homepage to kind of send people into the collection pages and get further down the funnel

args.text: An element is one of the highest-clicked on the page while very few people reach it.
args.quote: it was one of the highest clicked elements on the page but very few people were reaching there

completion.text: The source reports the A/B test showed an 18% result in conversions from that test alone.
completion.quote: with that AB test we saw an 18% uh in conversions just from that one um AB test alone

unknowns: Whether the 18% figure is a relative lift or percentage points is not stated, nor are test duration, sample size or statistical significance.
Click share (10.41%) and reach (30 to 35%) use different denominators: clicks versus people.

units.title: Clarity area maps judged easier to interpret than Hotjar engagement zones

claim.text: The source finds Hotjar's engagement zones more difficult to interpret and extract insights from compared with Microsoft Clarity's area maps.
claim.quote: I find this is a bit more difficult to interpret or extract insights from as compared to the area maps with Microsoft Clarity

args.text: In Hotjar, engagement zones are reached through the heat map's map types on the right-hand side and show where engagement is higher.
args.quote: if you go to the heat map and you click on map types if you go on the right hand side engagement zones you can kind of see where you know uh certain sections are where the engagement is higher

unknowns: This is the author's interpretive preference, not a measured comparison of the two features.

units.title: Run an exit-intent survey in Hotjar to capture why visitors leave

claim.text: The source says surveys are something Hotjar has that Microsoft Clarity does not have.
claim.quote: the other thing that hotter has the Microsoft Clarity doesn't have is the ability to conduct uh surveys on your website

action.text: Set up an exit-intent survey asking what stopped people from buying, what almost stopped them converting, or why they are exiting the site.
action.quote: you can set up exit intent surveys so for example asking people you know what stopped you from buying or you know what almost stopped you from converting today or what's kind of the reason that you're exiting the site

unknowns: The source says these surveys give a ton of insight and are voice of customer but gives no response-rate or sample guidance.
Hotjar survey responses are said to be limited, without the limit being specified.

units.title: Run post-purchase surveys in Hotjar to capture buying motivation

claim.text: The source says they often set up post-purchase surveys for clients, asking people right after they bought a product.
claim.quote: so we do this often for clients where we're literally asking people as soon as they bought a product

action.text: Ask post-purchase survey questions about what motivated the purchase and whether anything on the site almost stopped them from buying.
action.quote: the other thing that you can set up is postp purchase surveys so we do this often for clients where we're literally asking people as soon as they bought a product you know what motivated you to buy from us today right was there something on the site that almost stopped you from buying

unknowns: No guidance is given on when to trigger the post-purchase survey or on expected response volume.

units.title: Use Okendo for surveys on Shopify stores

claim.text: The source recommends a tool called Okendo for surveys.
claim.quote: what we actually recommend for heat Maps or sorry for surveys is a tool called okendo

action.text: Install Okendo on the site to collect unlimited responses, subject to the store's order data.
action.quote: you can install this on your site and you can collect unlimited responses unlike hot jar where you have a limit it just depends on your order data

args.text: Hotjar surveys add up in fees because the survey component is separate.
args.quote: this will tend to add up a lot in fees because the survey component of hot jar is actually a separate component

args.text: The store is a Shopify store.
args.quote: This is particularly for Shopify stores

unknowns: The source does not explain how response availability depends on the store's order data.
The source does not state which survey types Okendo supports relative to Hotjar's exit-intent and post-purchase surveys.

units.title: Use UserBrain for remote user testing instead of Hotjar's interview feature

claim.text: The source states UserBrain costs only $40 per tester, with an unclear trailing token.
claim.quote: this is only $40 per tester 4 Z

action.text: Set up remote user testing with UserBrain, asking first impressions on landing, walking through adding a product to the cart and checking out, or finding the contact form for a B2B site.
action.quote: with user brain you can basically set up remote user testing right so you're asking people what are your first impressions upon landing on the site can you go through the process of actually adding a product to your cart and checking out or you know finding the contract form if it's a B2B site

args.text: The source says they often end up using UserBrain instead of Hotjar.
args.quote: so often we end up using user brain instead of hotar

unknowns: '4 Z' after the $40 per tester price is unclear, and whether $40 is per tester per study or per session is not stated.
The source does not state whether UserBrain matches Hotjar's interview feature in capability.

units.title: Whether Hotjar's user interview feature is worth paying extra for

claim.text: The source calls Hotjar's user interview feature newer and says whether it is worth paying the extra money is arguable.
claim.quote: this is a newer feature to hotar again you know is it worth paying the extra money that's arguable

args.text: Hotjar offers the ability to conduct user interviews as one of its features.
args.quote: the other use case is you also have the ability to conduct user interviews with hotar it's right over here

unknowns: No resolution is given on whether Hotjar's user interviews justify their extra cost.
The price of Hotjar's user interview feature is not stated.

units.title: Set up custom funnels in Google Analytics 4 instead of Hotjar

claim.text: The source says Hotjar lets you set up custom funnels of how people are navigating through the site.
claim.quote: with hotar you know you're able to set up custom funnels as to how people are navigating through your site

action.text: Build the same custom funnel in Google Analytics 4 by going to the Explore tab.
action.quote: you can do this exact same thing with Google analytics 4 so if you go to Google analytics you go to the explore tab you can set up a custom funnel here

args.text: For example, a B2B company may want to see how many people go from homepage to contact form to thank-you page.
args.quote: if you're a B2B company you might want to see how many people go from your homepage to your contact form to actually your thank you page and filling out the form

args.text: The source notes GA4 already has this functionality built in.
args.quote: so again it's you know this is already functionality built in

unknowns: The source does not state whether GA4 funnels and Hotjar funnels report identical data or attribution.

units.title: Choose Hotjar if an all-in-one platform is required

claim.text: The source says that for an all-in-one platform with heatmaps, recordings, user interviews, surveys and funnels in one tool, Hotjar is the best bet, although a lot of those features are still paid for separately.
claim.quote: if you're looking for um a solution that contains an all-in-one platform right so the ability to look at heat Maps recordings uh user interviews surveys and funnels all in one Tool uh then hotra would be your best bet albeit you still have to pay separately for a lot of those features

unknowns: The source does not quantify which features require additional payment within Hotjar.

units.title: Choose Clarity for core heatmap and recording functionality

claim.text: The source says that for the core functionality most people want, namely heatmap data and watching recordings of users, Microsoft Clarity is the best bet.
claim.quote: if you're looking for the core functionality which you know majority of people are which is the ability to look at heat map data recording data watching recordings of users then you know Microsoft Clarity would be your best bet

unknowns: The no-data-limit and no-pricing basis for this recommendation is stated as of the time of recording.

units.title: Using Clarity alongside separate survey and user-testing tools

claim.text: The source says that if you are okay with using separate tools such as Okendo for surveys and UserBrain apart from the platform, there is no real downside and Microsoft Clarity would be the best bet.
claim.quote: you can also just you know if you're okay with using separate tools like the ones I mentioned okendo surveys and user brain separately from the platform there's no real downside to that then you know Microsoft Clarity would be your best bet

unknowns: The source does not address data integration or workflow overhead of running separate tools.

units.title: Hotjar pricing scales with traffic tier

claim.text: The source says the Hotjar Plus plan is $32 a month for 100 daily sessions, and that at higher numbers you tend to rack up quite a bill.
claim.quote: so for the Plus plan $32 a month which you get 100 daily sessions and then as you get to the higher numbers as well you tend to rack up quite a bill

args.text: Hotjar pricing depends on traffic and has different pricing tiers.
args.quote: depending on your traffic hot tier on the other hand right you have kind of you know different pricing tier

unknowns: The exact tier name is unclear because the transcript renders Hotjar as hot jar, hotra, hotar and hot tier.
The source does not state whether $32/month for 100 daily sessions is current pricing.

units.title: Hotjar surveys are a separately paid component

claim.text: The source says you have to pay additional for Hotjar surveys and feedback on top of the heatmap and recording software itself.
claim.quote: you have to pay additional for that for surveys and feedback in addition to the heat map and recording software itself

args.text: Considering Hotjar surveys for a site.
args.quote: the issue with the survey um with hotter in particular is that again you know this will tend to add up a lot in fees

unknowns: The amount of the additional Hotjar survey fee is not stated.

unresolved: The transcript garbles product names ('hot', 'hotra', 'hotar', 'hot D' for Hotjar; 'Heat MPP' for heatmap); units should be re-verified against the source if exact product naming or feature labels matter.
